It uses an 8x8 NeoPixel LED matrix as the display and six push buttons for control: two for each player's paddle movement, one to start the game, and one for reset. results.summary_before: This controller automatically switches the polarity of DC-type model railway turntables to prevent short circuits when rotating along powered tracks. It uses a binary counter and full-bridge control signals to reverse polarity, with error detection if a trigger remains active too long. The design requires external hardware including XOR gates, a full-bridge driver, MOSFETs, and an RC network for the oscillator. Testing involves verifying the counter sequence, polarity switching, and error handling as described in the documentation.
